seo_title: PFRDA Eases NPS KYC Address Proof for NRI Seafarers
title: PFRDA Relaxes Address-Proof Requirement for NRI Seafarers Opening NPS Tier I Accounts
court: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
case_name: PFRDA circular amending KYC requirements for NRI and OCI subscribers to the National Pension System
citation: PFRDA/2026/55/REG-POP/10, dated 13 November 2026, amending paragraph 8.3(a) of the KYC/AML/CFT Master Circular dated 25 September 2025 as earlier amended by PFRDA/2025/22/REG-POP/04 dated 2 December 2025
card_summary: PFRDA has relaxed the address-proof requirement NRI seafarers face when opening an NPS Tier I account. Seafarers often cannot produce the usual overseas address proof at onboarding, so the regulator now accepts an employment contract or discharge certificate instead. Identity verification and the other KYC due diligence steps stay unchanged, and the relaxation applies only to this one category of NRI subscriber.
card_tip: An NRI seafarer who cannot produce standard overseas address proof for an NPS account can now offer an employment contract or discharge certificate instead, though the other KYC documents are still required.
verification_notes: The circular number (PFRDA/2026/55/REG-POP/10), its date of 13 November 2026, the provision it amends (paragraph 8.3(a) of the 25 September 2025 KYC/AML/CFT Master Circular, as amended by the 2 December 2025 circular), the seafarer-specific address-proof relaxation, and the statement that other KYC requirements remain unchanged are confirmed across Taxguru, Angel One and Outlook Money, which agree on substance though they summarise the accepted documents slightly differently. This item serves the NRI audience named in the firm's current research priorities. The circular PDF itself was located but its full text beyond the amendment clause was not independently read line by line in this run, so the summary rests on the secondary reports read alongside it.
